newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Palestinians hope to clinch deal on Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Palestinians hope to clinch deal on Hebron.

text.p: Palestinian officials said on Saturday they hoped to clinch a deal on a long-delayed Israeli troop pullback from Hebron during next week's Middle East economic conference in Cairo.

Asked if agreement for an Israeli pullback from the West Bank town was nearing, Palestinian President Yasser Arafat's adviser Nabil Abu Rdainah said: "We hope to reach agreement under Egyptian and American sponsorship in Cairo."
He added that there were still critical issues that remained to be resolved.

Rdainah said that although Arafat would not attend the regional economic conference, he would meet Egyptian President Hosni Mubarak and U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher who are taking part in the 15-nation gathering.

"He (Arafat) will meet with President Mubarak and Christopher on Monday evening or Tuesday morning for further consultations to try to reach formulas to resolve the crisis of an Israeli troop redeployment from Hebron," Rdainah said.
Israel and the PLO are currently locked in U.S.-brokered negotiations on implementing an Israeli troop redeployment from the town of 100,000 Palestinians.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is seeking to modify the Hebron deal signed by the previous Labour-led government to safeguard the 400 Jewish settlers who live in the heart of the city. Palestinians reject any changes to the accord.
